### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 |
| **Summary** | De Gruyter Brill publisher-wide policy (no journal-specific AGPh page found): AI/ML tools cannot be listed as authors and papers 'generated by' AI are not accepted; authors declare no AI was used in drafting the manuscript text itself. However, if AI/ML tools were used as part of research design/methodology, use must be disclosed in Acknowledgments; disclosure required when AI output 'significantly contributed' to any manuscript part; simple proofreading/copy-editing with tools does not need declaration. Generative AI may not be used to create/manipulate images, figures, or research data. Authors are told not to paste manuscript text into AI systems (ChatGPT, Grammarly, etc.) over data-privacy concerns. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.degruyterbrill.com/publishing/for-authors/author-policies/artificial-intelligence |

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** History of philosophy across all periods from antiquity to the 20th century, published in English, German, French, and Italian; journal explicitly states it is expanding scope to include more research on non-Western histories of philosophy and non-canonical figures. Current volume is Subscribe-to-Open (S2O) open access, CC BY 4.0.

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** textual/exegetical history of philosophy, ancient philosophy (e.g. Plato/Timaeus reception), early modern philosophy (e.g. Thomasius, skepticism), German idealism / Neo-Kantianism (e.g. Natorp), history of ethics and rhetoric (e.g. Socratic studies), non-Western and non-canonical figures (stated growth area, not yet heavily represented in sampled recent titles)
